title: quintessentially pungent moroccan lamb tagine with kebabs
description: a hearty, pillowy moroccan stew with kefta-style lamb kebabs, richly flavored with scotch bonnet peppers and aromatic spices.

ingredients.name: lamb mince
ingredients.notes: preferably with a mix of lean and marbled meat

ingredients.name: cinnamon sticks
ingredients.notes: for added warmth in the tagine

instructions: heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. add the chopped onion and cook until it starts to brown.
add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the skillet and cook for 1 minute.
add the lamb mince to the skillet, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks. cook until the lamb is browned, then transfer it to a large bowl.
add the flour, salt, black pepper, cumin, coriander, and scotch bonnet peppers to the bowl with the lamb. mix well to combine.
form the lamb mixture into small kebabs and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
dot the top of each kebab with a little olive oil. bake in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until cooked through.
while the kebabs are cooking, prepare the tagine. heat a large, heavy-based pot over medium heat. add a little olive oil to the pot and then add the sliced green olives.
cook the olives for a few minutes until they start to soften, then add the chopped onion and cook until it starts to brown.
add the minced garlic and grated ginger to the pot and cook for 1 minute.
add the cinnamon sticks to the pot and cook for 2-3 minutes, or until fragrant.
add the lamb broth to the pot and bring to a simmer.
return the cooked kebabs to the pot and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the flavors have melded together and the meat is heated through.
serve the kebabs hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro if desired.
